newsitem.title: DUBAI: Number of Indians killed in haj fire rises to 94.
newsitem.headline: Number of Indians killed in haj fire rises to 94.

text.p: The number of Indian pilgrims killed when a fire swept through a tent camp in Saudi Arabia during the annual haj pilgrimage in April has risen to 94, an Indian embassy official said on Thursday.

"Those confirmed and identified as dead are now 94," he said. He said 174 injured Indian pilgrims were still in Saudi hospitals while 171 were being treated at the haj medical mission run by the Indian government in Mecca.
He said 127 Indian pilgrims were unaccounted for.
Indian officials had previously put the number of dead at 55, the injured at 354 and those missing at 247.
Saudi Arabia has said 343 died and more than 1,500 were injured in the April 15 blaze which raged through 70,000 tents at Mena near the Islamic holy city of Mecca.

Identifying bodies was difficult as many had been charred beyond recognition, diplomats said. Witnesses said many victims burned to death, others suffocated from the deadly fumes while some were crushed by a stampede as panic gripped the pilgrims.
About 80,000 Indians performed the haj, which is usually performed by two million Moslems each year.
Saudi Arabia has not announced what caused the fire saying it was an accident. Saudi media reports and witnesses had said they believed it was caused by pilgrims cooking in their tents.
Saudi Health Minister Osama bin Abdul-Majid Shobokshi was reported by Saudi media on Tuesday as saying up to 80 percent of the injured had left hospitals.
